blocks.label: Operational Guidelines
blocks.value: Never run destructive database migrations without verified read-replica snapshots and an automated rollback hook.

passages.text: For Kubernetes zero-downtime rollouts, configure maxSurge=25% and maxUnavailable=0 in Deployment specs. Ensure readiness probes have at least a 10s initial delay and 5s timeout to avoid dropping active in-flight requests during pod lifecycle transitions.

PostgreSQL connection pooling configuration: set PgBouncer pool_mode to transaction mode. Each application replica maintains max 20 connections to PgBouncer, which routes through 50 persistent server connections to the primary AWS RDS PostgreSQL 16 cluster.
Vault dynamic database credentials rotate every 60 minutes with a max lease TTL of 4 hours. Microservices renew leases at 50% TTL interval using the Vault agent sidecar injector.

Prometheus alerting threshold for memory leaks: trigger PagerDuty High alert when container_memory_working_set_bytes exceeds 85% of limit for 15 consecutive minutes, accompanied by container_memory_failures_total rate > 0.

recall_memory.text: Samantha, what is our approved command to roll back a failing Helm release in production staging?

Use `helm rollback <release-name> <revision-number> --namespace <ns> --wait --timeout 5m`. Always verify pod readiness status immediately afterwards with `kubectl rollout status deployment/<deployment-name>`.
Understood. We just verified revision 4 rollback successfully on cluster prod-east-2.
